title: China retail sales rise just 0.4% in October, investment falls
h1: China's retail sales grew only 0.4% in October and investment fell 8.1% this year, missing forecasts
description: China's October 2026 data, released November 16, show retail sales up 0.4%, factory output up 4.8% and fixed-asset investment down 8.1% for January to October.
standfirst: China's shoppers and factories both lost momentum in October, and investment kept shrinking. All three headline numbers came in below what analysts expected, adding to signs that the world's second-largest economy is leaning on exports.
keywords: China retail sales October 2026, China industrial output, China fixed-asset investment, National Bureau of Statistics, China economy slowdown, China property investment
takeaways: Retail sales rose 0.4% from a year earlier in October 2026, down from 1.1% in September and below the 0.8% analysts forecast, CNBC reported.
Industrial output grew 4.8%, compared with 5.5% in September and a 5.3% forecast.
Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1% in January through October, and real estate development investment fell 21.6%, China's statistics bureau said on November 16.
body: China's economy slowed on several fronts in October. Retail sales rose 0.4% from a year earlier, the National Bureau of Statistics said in its monthly release on Monday, November 16. That is down from 1.1% growth in September and below the 0.8% analysts had forecast, CNBC reported.
Factories also cooled. Industrial output grew 4.8% from a year earlier, compared with 5.5% in September. Analysts had expected 5.3%, according to CNBC.

Fixed-asset investment, which covers spending on things like buildings, equipment and infrastructure, fell 8.1% in the first ten months of the year. Analysts had expected a 7% drop, and CNBC described the slump as without precedent outside the Covid-19 period.

Property remains the heaviest drag. Investment in real estate development fell 21.6% over the same period, the bureau's figures show. Leaving property out, investment still fell 5.1%, and private investment was down 11.4%.

The urban surveyed unemployment rate was 5.1%, 0.1 percentage point lower than in September. Services output rose 4.6% from a year earlier. Trade stayed strong: the bureau put October exports at 28.7% above a year earlier in yuan terms.

The statistics bureau called the economy generally stable but acknowledged that supply at home is running well ahead of demand. That gap showed up in last week's price data, when consumer inflation came in at 0.7%.

China's economy grew 4.5% in the third quarter from a year earlier, CNBC reported, and Goldman Sachs expects 4.6% growth for all of 2026, down from 5% in 2025. Analysts at Citi Research said further European Union trade measures aimed at China look plausible, according to CNBC, as weak spending at home leaves Chinese factories relying more on sales abroad.
